title: Production governance: signoff templates, exception matrix, and SIEM field map
content:
Purpose:
This working doc collects: (A) a compact release signoff template for production-governance, (B) an exception-approval matrix for RBAC v2 / feature gates, (C) a lightweight SIEM export field map (canonical names + transformation notes) for release evidence, and (D) an automation checklist for collecting/verifying evidence prior to go-live.

Status and usage notes:
- Draft for internal review. Intended to be copied into release-specific release-pack (shiproom) and linked from the release checklist.
- This is intentionally concise; links to the canonical SIEM schema and audit-log spec are in linked_artifacts.
- TODO: align final field names with infra/schemas before first GA.

1) Quick signoff template (copy into release PR or shiproom message)
- Release name: <release-codename>
- Release owner (product): <name/email>
- Primary SRE owner: <name/email>
- Security approver: <name/email>  (must be from security team)
- RBAC v2 status: [green | amber | red]  -- attach RBAC export and policy diff
- Audit log schema validated: [yes/no]  -- attach sample events from staging SIEM export
- Evidence bucket (GCS/Azure): <path>  -- list of artifacts expected (see evidence checklist below)
- Exceptions requested: <short list>  -- reference exception IDs from matrix below
- Final approval (checkboxes):
  - Security review complete: [ ]
  - SRE rollback tested: [ ]
  - KMS/Key rotation reviewed: [ ]
  - Data residency verified: [ ]
  - Post-launch monitoring runbook present: [ ]
- Approvals:
  - Product owner: <sig>   date:
  - SRE owner: <sig>      date:
  - Security approver: <sig>  date:
  - Release manager: <sig> date:

2) Exception approval matrix (RBAC & audit gaps)
- Purpose: allow temporary or permanent exceptions with explicit compensating controls and TTLs.
- Columns (example): ID | Requester | Scope | Risk level | Proposed compensating controls | TTL | Reviewer | Status | Ticket
- Example row: EX-2025-71 | infra-team | cross-tenant service-account binding required for legacy-ingest | Medium | Enforce network egress filter + timeboxed key + alerting rule on SIEM | 30d | Security Senior | approved (conditional) | JIRA-SEC-893
- Approval tiers:
  - Low risk: Security engineer review + SRE acknowledgement (auto-approve after 48h if no objections)
  - Medium risk: Security lead + SRE lead signoff required
  - High risk: CISO or delegated exec signoff + mandatory mitigations + audit log retention extended
- Expiration and automation:
  - All exceptions must include a TTL and an automated reminder created in the release issue.
  - For exceptions longer than 90 days create a quarterly renewal ticket (owner assigned).

3) SIEM export & audit field map (practical checklist for release evidence)
- Goal: ensure the release produces the minimum set of structured events to validate RBAC changes, signer events, and fallback routing.
- Minimal event types to validate in staging export:
  - auth.grant (subject, actor, resource, role, grant_id, ttl, ts)
  - auth.revoke (subject, actor, resource, role, revoke_id, reason, ts)
  - svc.request (request_id, model, route, latency_ms, region, customer_id, ts)
  - svc.fallback (request_id, original_model, fallback_model, reason, ts)
  - keys.rotate (key_id, actor, old_key_hash, new_key_hash, ts)
  - error.exec (request_id, error_code, stack_tag, ts)

- Suggested canonical field names (mapping/transform notes):
  - actor -> user.email OR service.account (normalize into actor.identifier)
  - subject -> subject.id (user or service)
  - resource -> resource.path (model_repo:branch or endpoint id)
  - role -> rbac.role (string)
  - ts -> timestamp (ISO8601)
  - request_id -> trace.request_id (propagate across services)
  - latency_ms -> metrics.latency_ms (numeric)

- Export transform guidance (staging):
  - Export JSON lines with top-level fields: timestamp, event_type, event_version, payload (payload can be a flattened map). For the SIEM ingest team we recommended the following top-level keys: timestamp,event_type,event_version,actor,subject,resource,request_id,region,env
  - For older audit logs where actor is split into (actor_type, actor_id) include a mapping table in the release pack.

4) Evidence automation runbook (how to collect and attach items to the release pack)
- Step 0: Prepare an evidence bucket path (unique to release). Add release service account with read-only access.
- Step 1: RBAC export (command): rbac-cli export --version <v2-tag> --format json > rbac-export.json
  - Verify diff against previous prod: rbac-cli diff --base prod --head <release> > rbac-diff.txt
  - Attach rbac-export.json and rbac-diff.txt to evidence bucket.
- Step 2: SIEM sample export (30–60 minutes window during staged rollout): siem-export --query 'event_type in ("auth.grant","auth.revoke","svc.fallback")' --from <start> --to <end> --out siem-sample.json
  - Run a validate script that checks required fields are present (see minimal events above).
- Step 3: Key management proof: attach KMS key metadata (key_id, created_ts, rotation_policy). If keys rotated as part of release attach rotation log.
- Step 4: Automated smoke runs: run the post-deploy smoke harness (link to test harness) and collect structured output; attach smoke.log and smoke-output.json
- Step 5: Attach monitoring dashboards screenshots and the alert rules that will be enabled post-launch.
- Step 6: Upload all artifacts and paste evidence links into the release signoff template.

5) RBAC v2 gating checklist (pre-release)
- Are new roles scoped to least privilege? [Y/N]  (attach role definition summary)
- Are cross-tenant bindings approved? [Y/N]  (if Y attach exception ID)
- Is role inheritance documented and tested? [Y/N]
- Is policy compilation passing (no unreachable rules)? [Y/N]
- Has the RbacPolicy CI check passed for all changed repos? [Y/N] (link to CI run)
- Are ABAC attributes (if used) documented and sampled in policy tests? [Y/N]

6) Release/rollback coordination notes (short)
- Minimum rollback criteria: within 30 minutes of rollout start, if critical auth regressions are observed (e.g., auth.grant failing for service accounts used by ingestion), trigger rollback.
- SIEM check window: first 10 minutes after rollout must include at least 10 svc.request events and no more than 2 consecutive auth failures for the same service account.
- Communication: use #release-ops and tag @oncall-sre + @security when raising an exception or rollback. Template message included in linked_artifacts.

7) Open questions / TODOs (working list)
- Decide final retention period on prod SIEM exports used for release evidence (30/90/365 days).
- Add automated gating that queries SIEM and fails the release job if required events are missing (P0 work for infra).
- Finalize field normalization for "actor" vs "subject" across services.

Appendix: sample quick Slack approval text (copy/paste)
"Release <release-codename> is ready for prod signoff. Security review: RBAC v2 export attached (rbac-export.json). SIEM sample included. Exceptions: EX-2025-71 (approved conditional). Approvers: @marisol (security), @avery (sre). Reply with \"sg\" to approve or raise objection within 48h."

End of doc.
